questions.stem: The chemical name of 'common salt' used in cooking is:
questions.explanation: Common salt = sodium chloride (NaCl). Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) — baking soda; sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) — washing soda; sodium hydroxide (NaOH) — caustic soda. Indian table salt is fortified with potassium iodate to prevent goitre. Sea water is ~3.5 % NaCl by weight; Sambhar Lake and Rann of Kachchh are important sources of salt in India.

questions.explanation: Quicklime — CaO — made by heating limestone (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂). On adding water — exothermic slaking to give calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂), 'slaked lime', used in whitewashing. Lime water is a dilute solution of Ca(OH)₂; turns milky on passing CO₂ (that's the basic chemistry test for CO₂).

questions.stem: 'Dry ice' — used in cold storage and stage smoke — is the solid form of:
questions.explanation: Dry ice — solid CO₂. Sublimes directly to gas at −78.5 °C at standard pressure (does not melt — hence 'dry'). Used to keep ice cream and frozen foods cold during transit, for rapid cooling in lab work, and for stage 'smoke' effects (fog comes from water condensing around the cold CO₂ vapour). Liquid nitrogen is colder (−196 °C) but is liquid, not solid, at its boiling point.

questions.stem: 'Vinegar' is a dilute aqueous solution of:
questions.explanation: Vinegar — 4-8 % acetic acid (CH₃COOH) in water. Made by the bacterial fermentation of ethanol. Citric acid is in lemons and limes (not vinegar); oxalic acid in spinach and some rust-removers; HCl in stomach acid (toxic at vinegar-level concentrations on skin). Acetic acid gives pickles and chutneys their sour taste and preserves food. ethanoic acid.

questions.stem: 'Marble' — used in buildings like the Taj Mahal — is a rock form of:
questions.explanation: Marble — a metamorphic rock, chiefly calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), formed from limestone under heat and pressure. Because it is a carbonate, it reacts with acids — which is why acid rain (H₂SO₄, HNO₃) is eating into the Taj Mahal's white Makrana marble. Silicon dioxide — quartz / sand. Iron oxide — rust. Aluminium silicate — the mineral base of common clays.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: 'Bleaching powder' — widely used to disinfect water and to bleach cotton — has the chemical name:
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder — CaOCl₂ / more precisely a mixture that contains calcium hypochlorite Ca(OCl)₂ — produced by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime. Releases Cl₂, which is the active bleaching / disinfecting agent. Used in paper and textile mills for bleaching, and in municipal water treatment and swimming pools. Liquid bleach (in laundries) is sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) solution.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: 'Gypsum' — used to make plaster of Paris — is chemically:
questions.explanation: Gypsum — CaSO₄·2H₂O. Heated to around 120 °C, it loses 1.5 water molecules to give plaster of Paris — CaSO₄·½H₂O. When PoP is mixed with water again, it sets within minutes as it re-crystallises into gypsum. Widely used in medical casts, decorative mouldings, blackboard chalk. Pure gypsum also occurs in nature as selenite crystals.
